patients.summary: Retired teacher in Florence with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and long-standing RA on methotrexate/prednisone, treated breast cancer, who over six years develops osteoporosis, ulcerative colitis, bone-only metastatic breast cancer recurrence, right femoral head AVN, bisphosphonate jaw osteonecrosis, sigmoid diverticulitis, a stage I colon cancer found on follow-up colonoscopy, and a postoperative pulmonary embolism.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

65 y/o retired elementary school teacher transferring primary care to us from a practice she has been with for many years. Wants one office that keeps track of all her specialists. Lives in Florence.

Problems she brings:
- HTN, long-standing. HCTZ 25 qAM + amlodipine 5. Checks BP at the pharmacy occasionally, "usually in the 120s."
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 20 qHS, no side effects.
- Rheumatoid arthritis for years, followed by an outside rheumatology group every 6 months. On methotrexate 15 mg weekly (Saturdays), folic acid daily, prednisone 5 mg daily. Hands "good most days." Rheum gets her monitoring labs through her PCP's lab; will continue that here.
- Breast cancer 2016, treated with surgery and nodal staging at an outside cancer center, finished treatment. Sees oncology yearly with a mammogram.

PSH: L breast lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy 2016.
Meds: as above, reconciled from her bottles.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother had breast cancer after menopause and broke a hip in her 70s. Father had colon cancer. Sister has RA.
SH: Quit cigarettes in 2013. 1-2 glasses of wine a week. No other substances. Taught second and third grade for decades, now retired. Drives, manages her own household and medications.
Screening per patient: colonoscopy in 2018 with prior practice, told it was normal and to repeat in 5 yrs given her father. Has not had a bone density test that she can recall.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, edema. No GI complaints. Some morning stiffness in hands <30 min. Weight stable.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP fine on current regimen. Well appearing woman in no distress. HEENT unremarkable, dentition fair. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts deferred to oncology. Hands: no synovitis today. No edema. Skin without rash.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension - controlled. Continue HCTZ and amlodipine. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin; lipid panel.
3. RA on MTX/prednisone - CBC w diff and CMP today, then every ~3 months for rheum. Long-term steroid use noted; bone density will be due, will order at her wellness visit.
4. Hx breast cancer - oncology surveillance continues; get their notes.
5. Health maintenance - Tdap today (last unknown). Hep C and HIV screening once, ordered. Flu shot when available next month. Welcome-to-Medicare/AWV early next year.
6. Records release signed for prior practice.

RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Ms. Jacobs,

Your labs from Monday all came back fine. Blood counts, liver and kidney tests (the ones we watch with methotrexate) are normal, and your LDL cholesterol is at goal on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative; those are one-time tests and don't need repeating.

I'll send your results along to your rheumatologist as well. Next methotrexate labs are due in early December.

- your primary care physician

documents.title: Prior primary care records - summary
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior primary care office (64 pages). Scanned to media. Abstracted for PCP review:

- Problem list: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, rheumatoid arthritis, history of left breast cancer (2016).
- Breast: 2016 left lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy at an outside cancer center; treatment completed; surveillance by oncology.
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal exam, repeat 5 years (family history).
- Meds on last list: HCTZ 25, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg, prednisone 5 mg. Matches our reconciliation.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations: influenza yearly through 2019. No pneumococcal or zoster vaccines documented.
- No DXA on file.

Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. Consistent with what she told me. Due for repeat colonoscopy 2023. Needs DXA (age, chronic prednisone). Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines not on record - plan at upcoming visits. Nothing urgent.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Nurse visit for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions. VIS reviewed. Fluzone High-Dose given IM left deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated without issue, waited 15 min.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison with prior outside studies. Personal history of left breast cancer treated with lumpectomy. Breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. Post-lumpectomy architectural distortion and surgical clips in the left breast, stable. No suspicious mass, calcifications or new distortion in either breast. Skin and axillae unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Stable post-treatment changes of the left breast. No mammographic evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS 2: benign. Annual mammography recommended.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Re: Arlene Jacobs, DOB 1955-01-30
Visit date: 11/12/2020

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Jacobs today for routine follow-up of her rheumatoid arthritis. She is happy to hear she has established with your office and that her monitoring labs will be drawn there.

She reports about 20 minutes of morning stiffness in the hands, no flares since spring, and is fully active. On exam there is no synovitis today in the wrists, MCPs or PIPs. Labs from September reviewed and are unremarkable.

Assessment: RA, low disease activity on current regimen.
Plan:
- Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily.
- Continue prednisone 5 mg daily.
- CBC and CMP every 3 months.
- Return in 6 months.

Thank you for allowing me to share in her care.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC/CMP for MTX monitoring normal. Copy to rheum. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: COVID shots
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I got both of my Pfizer shots at the community clinic at the high school, January 22 and February 12. Second one made me tired for a day but that's all. Can you put them in my record? I have the card if you need a picture. Also should I hold my methotrexate around these? My rheumatologist's office said one week but I forgot to ask before the second one. Thank you, Arlene

documents.title: RE: COVID shots
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Arlene, both doses are now entered in your chart. The one-week hold after each dose is what rheumatology recommends; since the second dose is already done there's nothing more you need to do. Glad it went smoothly.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

HRA reviewed. Lives independently, manages finances and medications herself, drives. No falls in the past 12 months, no fear of falling. Hearing and vision adequate with readers. Advance directive: discussed; she will think about naming a health care proxy.

Functional/cognitive: no concerns from patient; conversation and recall normal.
Depression screen PHQ-2 = 0.
Alcohol: 1-2 drinks/week.

Vitals as charted.
Brief exam: well appearing. Lungs clear, heart regular. Gait steady, gets up from chair without using arms.

Prevention plan:
- DXA ordered - age and years of prednisone.
- Shingrix #1 today (ok on MTX, non-live). #2 in 2-6 months.
- Pneumococcal: PCV20 in the fall with her flu shot.
- Colonoscopy due 2023 (5-yr interval, father with colon cancer).
- Mammography with oncology yearly.
- MTX labs drawn today.

Written prevention schedule given.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: DXA of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. Indication: postmenopausal, chronic glucocorticoid therapy. No prior study for comparison. L1-L4 BMD T-score -3.0. Left femoral neck T-score -2.0. Left total hip T-score -1.6. No vertebral levels excluded.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis by WHO criteria at the lumbar spine (T-score -3.0). Low bone mass at the left hip. Recommend repeat in 2 years on therapy.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once weekly on Sunday morning with a full glass of water, 30 minutes before food; stay upright

documents.title: DXA results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with DXA: lumbar spine T -3.0, hip -1.6 to -2.0. This is osteoporosis, likely postmenopausal plus years of prednisone. Discussed treatment. She'd like to start a weekly pill rather than an infusion.

Plan:
- Alendronate 70 mg weekly; reviewed how to take it (empty stomach, full glass of water, upright 30 min). No reflux or swallowing problems. Teeth: sees her dentist twice a year, no planned dental work.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg/vitamin D3 400 IU twice daily.
- Referral to endocrinology given steroid exposure.
- Repeat DXA 2 yrs.

Rx sent. She will ask her dentist at next cleaning about anything she should know.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB: 01/30/1955   Date of visit: 05/10/2021
Reason for referral: osteoporosis

Thank you for referring Ms. Jacobs, a 66-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on chronic low-dose prednisone, found on DXA in March to have a lumbar spine T-score of -3.0 with a femoral neck T-score of -2.0. She started weekly alendronate two months ago and is taking it correctly without GI upset. She has had no fractures as an adult. Mother fractured a hip in her early 70s.

Medications reviewed, including prednisone 5 mg daily and methotrexate. Calcium/vitamin D twice daily.

Exam: pleasant, no kyphosis, no spinal tenderness. Height today matches your office's measurement.

Impression: postmenopausal osteoporosis with a glucocorticoid contribution, no fragility fractures.

Recommendations:
1. Continue alendronate 70 mg weekly. Good choice as first-line therapy.
2. Continue calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 twice daily; dietary calcium is fair.
3. Encourage weight-bearing exercise and fall precautions.
4. Repeat DXA in two years; I will see her then with calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, TSH and 25-OH vitamin D beforehand.
5. Keep the prednisone dose as low as rheumatology can manage.

Endocrinology

Meds reviewed, no changes. No dizziness, no leg swelling.

O: Vitals as charted, BP at goal. Lungs clear, heart RRR. No edema.
Labs 6/7: CBC/CMP normal, LDL 90s on atorvastatin 20.

A/P:
- HTN: controlled on HCTZ/amlodipine, continue.
- HLD: at goal, continue atorvastatin 20.
- Osteoporosis: on alendronate + Ca/D. DXA again 2023.
- RA: MTX labs up to date, next due September.
RTC 6 months, flu/PCV20 in October.

documents.title: Lab review

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu (L deltoid) and Prevnar 20 (R deltoid) given per PCP order. Pt on methotrexate - per standing guidance no hold needed for these inactivated vaccines. Tolerated well. PCV20 completes her pneumococcal series.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 10/2020. Scattered fibroglandular density. Left breast lumpectomy site with clips and stable architectural distortion. No new mass, suspicious calcification or distortion in either breast.
reports.conclusion: Benign post-surgical changes left breast, unchanged. BI-RADS 2: benign. Continue annual mammography.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Re: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Seen 10/28/2021

Ms. Jacobs returns for RA follow-up. She has had no flares since spring; stiffness is brief. She is now on alendronate for osteoporosis, which I was glad to see.

Exam: no synovitis today; full fist bilaterally. Labs from September normal.

Plan: no change. Methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid, prednisone 5 mg daily. Quarterly CBC/CMP through your office. Return in 6 months.

Rheumatology
